key_insight: Detonation-spray settings control the roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity of titanium dioxide–based coatings, enabling optimization for maximum water repellency.
engineering_relevance: Process–property equations can guide spray-parameter selection to achieve desired coating geometry and surface wetting behavior.
method: Vary detonation-spray conditions, including nozzle travel speed and spray distance.
Evaluate coating roughness, thickness, and water contact angle.
Derive predictive equations and identify conditions for maximum hydrophobicity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports inverse-power relationships between nozzle speed and both roughness and thickness, plus parabolic relationships between spray distance and both roughness and contact angle.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical optimum, tested parameter ranges, or prediction errors, limiting direct transfer to production.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
